title: Post-shift Reflections: on-call & SLOs (2026-08-29)
content:
Context and purpose:
This note captures the on-call reflection meeting after the Friday night rotation (Mid-Atlantic region). Goal: identify quick wins and follow-ups from incidents, sanity-check SLO signals, and refine handoff content for the next shift. Informal; meant to sit alongside ticketed follow-ups (see linked JIRA tickets).

Summary (TL;DR):
- Two distinct incidents handled during the shift: a tokenization service OOM (partial degradation) and a regional ingress throttling that produced elevated 504 rates for hosted-api customers in us-east-1 for ~18m. No customer-facing data loss.
- 95th percentile chat latency SLO breached temporarily: baseline 250ms target, observed spike to ~380ms at peak during the ingress issue.
- On-call runbook gaps surfaced: missing roll-forward steps for the lightweight tokenizer, unclear autoscaler escalation thresholds.
- Action items created: SRE-4217 (tokenizer config pin + memory guard), SRE-4218 (autoscaler threshold audit), SRE-4219 (add synthetic canary to detect ingress queueing earlier).

Incident 1 — tokenizer-worker OOM (22:14–22:42 UTC)
- Symptoms: rapid increase in tokenization worker process memory followed by repeated restarts on two nodes in the serving-pool (gpu-pool-b). Observed elevated 5xx counts on short-lived generation requests.
- Immediate mitigation: cordoned two affected nodes, scaled up a spare pool with lighter quantized model slices, and applied temporary memory-limit cap on the tokenizer sidecar (hotfix patch via GH PR 1983).
- Root cause hypothesis: recent change in tokenizer library (nlp-tokenizer v1.4.0) introduced a pathological allocation with long-payload prompts (>8k chars). The change was rolled in via canary earlier that day but the canary sample did not include long-payload traffic.
- Follow-ups: pin tokenizer to v1.3.7 for dedicated pools until allocator fix (SRE-4217), add integration test covering long-payload prompts to CI, update canary input set to include long-payload examples.

Incident 2 — regional ingress throttling (02:03–02:21 UTC)
- Symptoms: elevated 504 gateway timeouts originating from the edge-to-ingress queue in us-east-1. Client-side retries spiked, causing downstream amplification into the serving runtime.
- Detection: first alert fired on edge-queue-depth > 95th of baseline and correlated 504 rate >2.5% for the region. The alert took ~3m to hit human eyes due to Slack alert grouping (tweak in alert routing noted).
- Mitigation: temporarily rebalanced traffic to secondary region (us-west-2), increased ingress worker concurrency cap, and enabled the fast-fail policy for requests exceeding queue depth thresholds.
- Postmortem notes: a networking flakiness in our load-balancer tier coincided with a traffic burst from a partner integration test. We need better isolation for partner traffic and a plan to throttle noisy tenants at the edge.
- Follow-ups: SRE-4218 for autoscaler thresholds and a throttle-by-tenant feature request (linked to product). Also schedule a tabletop with edge infra to review L4/L7 failover timing.

SLOs and metrics snapshot:
- Chat latency SLO (p95): target 250ms; observed 95th: pre-incident 240ms, peak 380ms, recovered to 230ms within 10m of mitigation.
- Error budget: 0.5% monthly budget remaining for chat-service; after this incident estimated burn ~0.04% (within budget but trend watch).
- Tokenization success rate: brief drop to 96% from baseline 99.8% during OOM window.
- Synthetic canaries: the existing canary did not cover long-payload tokenization — planned to extend.

Handoff notes (for next on-call):
- Current on-call: Diego A. (ending), next on-call: Sara G. (starts 2026-08-29 08:00 UTC).
- Key context to pass: tokenization pinned to v1.3.7 for gpu-pool-b, hotfix deployed (PR 1983) to add memory limit; autoscaler policy temporarily bumped but revert scheduled after review (open: SRE-4218).
- Where to find runbooks: Confluence runbook link in linked_artifacts. Patch and rollback playbooks exist but need a new entry for long-payload detection.
- Escalation list: includes contacts for edge infra, serving runtime lead (Liam Chen), and product owner for partner integrations.

What went well:
- Fast coordination between on-call and serving-runtime: deployment of hotfix took ~12 minutes from diagnosis to rollout on a guarded pool.
- Canary rollback policies worked as intended where canaries were triggered.
- Cross-team escalation (edge infra) was timely once Slack alert grouping was manually expanded.

What could be improved / open questions:
- Canary coverage: we must expand canary input diversity (long payloads, noisy-partner patterns). Who owns the canary corpus? (Action: Diego to propose update by 2026-09-02).
- Alert routing cadence: grouped alerts delayed attention initially — evaluate moving some critical alert routes to phone/SMS for night shifts (SRE-4220).
- Autoscaler audit: threshold tuning and safety caps need docs and tests. Is there room to do automated synthetic overload testing in staging to derive safe thresholds?

Action items (owners & ETA):
- SRE-4217: Pin tokenizer to v1.3.7 for dedicated pools; create CI test for long-payload tokenization. Owner: Priya K. ETA: 2026-09-03.
- SRE-4218: Autoscaler threshold audit + proposed safe defaults and temporary revert plan. Owner: Liam C. ETA: 2026-09-06.
- SRE-4219: Add synthetic canary for ingress queue depth and long-payload tokenization. Owner: Diego A. ETA: 2026-09-02.
- SRE-4220: Review alert routing for critical region-level failures; propose new on-call communication channels for night shifts. Owner: Sara G. ETA: 2026-09-01.

Notes to self / informal reminders:
- Add a short checklist to the on-call handoff doc: "recent canaries run / pinned libs / pending reverts" — reduces cognitive load for incoming on-call.
- Consider a small runbook subsection: "If P95 chat latency > 300ms AND ingress 504s > 1% -> consider region failover" (we had to make this decision fast tonight).

Appendix (raw signals & links):
- Timeline snippet: 22:10 detect memory rise -> 22:14 first restart -> 22:18 cordon and scale up spare -> 22:26 deploy hotfix -> 22:42 system stable
- Edge incident timeline: 02:01 unusual partner spike -> 02:03 alert -> 02:08 triage -> 02:12 traffic rebalance -> 02:21 full recovery
- Useful links: Confluence runbook (linked), GitHub PR 1983 (hotfix), JIRA SRE-4217/4218/4219/4220

If anything is unclear in the morning please ping me directly (Priya) or check the on-call thread in #sre-oncall. This note will be converted into action tickets if accepted by owners in the morning sync.

End of notes.
